result.title: PhysCodeGym: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Physically Verifiable 4D Reconstruction
result.summary: Building physical simulations from video requires coding agents to translate observations into executable models and refine them through tool use. We introduce PhysCodeGym, a benchmark for physically verifiable 4D reconstruction with $156$ tasks covering rigid-body, liquid, deformable, and wind-driven motion. Agents autonomously inspect videos, write and run Blender programs, and revise their scenes using simulation feedback. Six metrics combine rule-based measurements with rubric-based judgments to assess visual and physical reconstruction quality. Program inspection, scene measurements, and counterfactual interventions test physical consistency under original and modified conditions. Experiments with frontier coding agents reveal a tradeoff between artifact quality and completion across reasoning-effort settings, while harness comparisons and agent traces link verification behavior with reconstruction performance. Case studies show that matching visible objects and events can coexist with physical defects. Counterfactual tests further expose latent contact and support failures in reconstructions that pass ordinary physical checks, highlighting the gap between reproducing observations and building reliable physical models. Code is available at https://github.com/ShaoShuai0605/PhysCodeGym.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 PhysCodeGym，一个面向可物理验证 4D 重建的编码代理基准，含 156 个刚体、液体、可形变与风驱动任务，代理自行查看视频、编写并运行 Blender 程序，依据模拟反馈迭代场景，并用六项指标与反事实干预检验重建质量。
AI.relevance_reason: 其反事实干预与 agent trace、harness 对比可能为 LVR 中验证行为、证据获取与停止决策的评价提供线索，但研究对象是编码代理的物理重建，与 latent 推理状态生成和使用无直接联系。
